answer.rationale: Leadership seeks an urgent response to competitive pricing pressure. Memory_73 explicitly warns against generalizing promotional pricing—it caused material 30-day retention loss despite acquisition lift, exactly the wrong signal when churn is already doubling. A direct price war mirrors the competitor's play and sacrifices margin on the install base. Instead, activate existing at-risk SMB accounts faster through in-product messaging (memory_91: +11% week-one engagement, +6% activation, +1% retention) combined with simplified onboarding (memory_86: +13% completion, -2.1 days time-to-value, +3% retention). This addresses the root friction that makes price-sensitive accounts vulnerable to competitive switching: slow time-to-value and low early engagement. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well in established cohorts but won't help retain at-risk SMBs today. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to SMB churn. A standard_experiment scale allows rapid deployment with measured guardrails while preserving margin and avoiding broad retention damage. This preserves the optionality to escalate if churn stabilizes or to add pricing moves only if activation gains prove insufficient.
